question: The voltage regulation in percentage for transformer is given by:
solution:
The correct answer is __Voltage regulation =frac{V{ₙₒₗₒₐd}-V{ₗₒₐd}}{V{ₗₒₐd}}×100.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Voltage regulation__ is an important parameter in transformer performance.
 
• The formula determines the change in voltage from no load to full load conditions.
 
• The regulation is expressed in percentage to indicate the efficiency of the transformer.
 
• Lower voltage regulation values indicate better transformer performance.
 
• This formula is specifically used for calculating the percentage regulation under load conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Transformer Efficiency:**
 
 
• Efficiency is determined by the ratio of output power to input power.
 
• High-efficiency transformers minimize energy losses.
 
 
 
• **Load Conditions:**
 
 
• Voltage regulation varies depending on load type (resistive, inductive, or capacitive).
 
• Inductive loads typically result in higher voltage drops.
 
 
 
• **No-Load Voltage:**
 
 
• It is the voltage measured at the secondary terminal when there is no load connected.
 
• No-load voltage is typically higher than full-load voltage.
